Reproduce the PAC Explorer integration and startup stability fix

Upstream: https://github.com/kyle-annora/annora-explorer
Exact starting commit: 8977d5cd4e314f344bcdd086684550b827efc8cb
Use a clean checkout of that commit. Apply the accompanying integration.patch ONCE from its root with git apply /absolute/path/to/integration.patch. This is the complete cumulative patch; do not first apply an earlier PAC patch. Local upstream README/pilot documentation changes are excluded.

With Node 22.13 or newer, install the pinned package-lock dependencies using npm ci, then run npm run verify. Copy the complete dist/ directory to the PAC project's assets/explorer/ directory and serve at /explorer/. Retain all model and third-party license files. For GitHub Pages, the PAC project's static exporter adapts only the generated deployment prefix and browser-storage namespace. It does not modify this upstream checkout.

Cumulative changes
- /explorer/ build base.
- Same-origin annoraDemoHost departure hook: await beforeLeave() before removing the iframe; only true permits removal. Seller uses its native Keep editing / Discard edits / Save & continue dialog; buyer saves through its existing lifecycle. isDirty() and isBusy() are synchronous.
- Mobile Changed label stays on one line.
- Route-aware viewer Retry resumes the pending saved inquiry without confirming or duplicating records.
- Startup-only foreground budgets cover iframe opening/readiness (45 seconds), handshake (12 seconds), and the two hydration queries (30 seconds). Hidden, persisted pagehide, freeze and print events suspend these budgets without resetting them. Initial valid messages/errors are still accepted while hidden; retries resume with an immediate hello. Ordinary commands and bounded disposal keep their wall-clock deadlines.
- Terminal viewer failure rejects late iframe loads; it cannot emit a contradictory ready callback.
- Eight departure/retry regression cases plus 26 startup cases; the existing lifecycle listener assertion reflects the added scope.

Actual rendered-frame readiness, renderer, model geometry, quote permissions and review/confirmation gates are unchanged. The startup fix corrects reproduced mechanisms; it does not establish a cause or universal fix for every historical visible cold-start stall. Native print lifecycle behavior still needs target-browser verification. No network delivery or real quotation is introduced.

Verification for this source: npm run verify passed 1,036 tests, zero failures, one existing skip (1,037 total), with all three builds successful. Source/model/license provenance and final artifact hashes are in build-provenance.json. The prior public release remains preserved in PAC Git main 98f014a56695c0308c0460e4fb8fb09cacb2b757 and gh-pages 39039e3189b823789a96d2468122bc5162c99ed7. This task does not push or deploy.

PAC homepage nameplate adapter (7 November 2026)
The PAC app additionally owns assets/explorer/pac-entry.js and pac-branding.js.
index.html uses pac-entry.js instead of directly starting the unchanged upstream
explorer-DjmcOZCN.js bundle. The entry installs a small AssemblyScene adapter only
for ?branding=pac, requested by Website's homepage. It applies the existing PAC
logo as a textured nameplate on the reference mechanism's front deck; this is an
illustrative brand treatment, not PAC CAD. The mesh follows the parent and is
included in renderer captures. Original geometry, animations and licenses remain
unchanged. Reapply these two local files and the index entry after upstream copies.
The build-provenance.json describes the upstream artifact before this local adapter;
it is not a checksum assertion for the adapted index or the added files. Verify
export aliases, deck geometry and load/disposal hooks when upgrading the vendor.
